proposal.summary: All six components the researcher packet treated as "current winners" (otelcol-contrib, prometheus, loki, grafana, restic, sandbox-runtime) earn their place on freshly checked, mostly-native evidence -- but the catalog's own bookkeeping (layers.json / catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json, checked_at 2026-09-22) actually records "winners": [] and "verdict_status": "pending_lanes", not a clean six-item list. Reading the actual adjudication file (evidence/artifacts/layer-verdicts-20260922/adjudication/us-equities-observability-hosting-20260922.json) shows why: it was a forced choice between two 2-component additions to otelcol-contrib -- set A (prometheus+loki) vs set B (sandbox-runtime+restic) -- and all 4 judgments split exactly along presentation order ("each... chose whichever return was shown as A"), a documented order-bias artifact, not an evidence disagreement; every judge's own text calls all four candidates well-evidenced. Grafana was in neither contested set (both lanes already agreed on it). Since prometheus/loki (telemetry storage) and sandbox-runtime/restic (sandbox+backup) answer different, non-overlapping scope terms the requirement names, the merit-based resolution is to keep all four together rather than pick a pair -- that alone resolves the "lanes disagreed" open_gap without new evidence. Two independent-verification findings during this review change the substantive picture: (1) restic's proven scope is broader than the researcher packet says -- two dated 2026-09-19 native_cli_e2e receipts I read directly (state-recovery/memory and state-recovery/qdrant, already cited by landscape/us-equities.json but omitted by the researcher) show live ai-memory SQLite and live Qdrant backup+restore with full integrity verification, not just the 22 static files the packet cites; off-host durability and Loki/Prometheus/broker-journal backup remain the real, still-open pieces. (2) I re-read the sandbox-runtime network-denial receipt myself rather than trusting the adversarial stage's account, and it holds up (dated 2026-09-25, independent review by a separately identified claude-opus-5-5 session, both "agree") -- but it tests generic loopback-HTTP egress denial, not "broker execution authority" specifically, which is this layer's own requirement text and the one clause no candidate has yet demonstrated. Separately, this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep already ran two adversarial-review lenses over three candidates this task's researcher packet never mentioned: Grafana Tempo (survived, not refuted -- a real gap, since Claude Code already emits OTLP trace spans nothing currently ingests) and Presidio / Vector.dev (both refuted, with concrete reasons). The researcher packet also omitted Langfuse entirely despite it already being tracked as an "alternative" in this repo's own catalog. Net proposal: keep all six winners; add Grafana Tempo as a bounded trial candidate for the undemonstrated tracing gap; run the two concrete tests still open (re-validate the existing fixture against Prometheus v3.15.0 before bumping the pin one point release; exercise broker-execution-authority denial specifically, the missing half of sandbox-runtime's own overturn arm); leave the LLM-trace-observability candidates (Opik/SigNoz/Langfuse/Phoenix) as watch-only since none has native evidence and none beats an incumbent on this layer's actual scope. None of this moves a paper-lane number (engines run / paper acts passed / paper fills) -- it is infrastructure for the research harness itself, not the trading path.

winner_status.note: Pin v0.161.0 (2026-09-15) matches upstream latest exactly; repo active (pushed 2026-09-26), Apache-2.0, not archived -- per GitHub API. Native-proven: `otelcol-contrib validate` exits 0 and the collected usage histogram matches native Codex/Claude task totals (observability/receipt.json). Correction carried over from the adversarial stage: delivery to Loki is not via a dedicated lokiexporter component (absent from the v0.161.0 distribution manifest; deprecated upstream, issue #33916) but via the generic OTLP exporter into Loki's own OTLP/structured-metadata ingestion -- the single-binary claim holds, the named mechanism doesn't. Real open item, found in this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep and independently confirmed by me reading observability/receipt.json directly: the collector's persistent spool has 'no automatic expiry' and 'no loss/recovery acceptance under full disk or extended backend outage.' Vector.dev was investigated as a fix and adversarially refuted (would duplicate the pipeline; its own docs say its disk buffers force-exit on disk-full) -- the correct next step is fault-testing the existing collector's own queue, not adopting a second tool. Also still missing: a trace backend (see Tempo below).

Pin v3.14.0 is one point release behind upstream v3.15.0 (released 2026-09-25) -- routine drift on an actively maintained project (66k+ stars, pushed 2026-09-26), not a quality signal. Re-run the existing observability/backends fixture against 3.15.0 before moving the pin rather than assuming compatibility. Native-proven: usage-histogram total 40518 matched via Prometheus query; prometheus_historical_sample=true after a Collector/backend restart.

Pin v3.7.8 matches upstream latest exactly; no drift. AGPL-3.0 self-host-only constraint already accepted, not a new gap. Native-proven: loki_log=true after restart; LogQL sum 121288 exactly equals the receipt's own recorded arithmetic (80770 prior + 40518 fresh).

Notably absent from both contested sets in the 2026-09-22 adjudication (set A = otelcol-contrib+prometheus+loki, set B = otelcol-contrib+sandbox-runtime+restic) -- both lanes retained it without dispute, so the layer's empty-winners bookkeeping doesn't actually implicate Grafana. Pin v13.2.2 matches upstream latest exactly. Native-proven dashboard render plus post-restart datasource acceptance. One minor provenance note on file, not a functional gap: the installed packaged binary's build commit differs from the v13.2.2 git tag's commit (backends/receipt.json: grafana_tag_build_commit_equal=false) -- worth closing given this repo's security-supply-chain layer already flags unverified build provenance/signatures as an open item there.

The researcher/adversarial packet's framing ('covers static public files only -- no live SQLite/Qdrant/Loki/Prometheus database... backed up,' citing only blueprints/us-equities/hosting/backup/receipt.json) is stale. I independently found and read two further native_cli_e2e receipts on current main (git log: commit 8f1da517) that the packet never cited but that this repo's own landscape/us-equities.json (checked 2026-09-22) already cites for this exact candidate: state-recovery/memory/receipt.json (2026-09-19, live ai-memory SQLite online-backup through encrypted restic backup/check --read-data('no errors were found')/restore --verify plus an isolated bwrap-sandboxed application restore -- integrity_check ok, 0 FK violations, all 56 tables and FTS counts matching) and state-recovery/qdrant/receipt.json (2026-09-19, live Qdrant snapshot through the same restic chain, byte-identical, 'no errors were found,' isolated native restore reproducing 5/5 collections, 201/201 points and an exact query result). Live-database backup+restore is therefore established for ai-memory and Qdrant specifically, contrary to the packet's blanket claim. What remains genuinely open across all three restic receipts I read: off-host durability (off_host:false / repository and password share a host, in every one) and Loki/Prometheus/broker-order-journal live-state backup (covered by none).

Pin v0.0.77 matches upstream latest exactly; repo active, Apache-2.0. I independently re-read evidence/hosts/nativestack-5975wx-20260925/...sandbox-runtime--use--20260925.json myself rather than only trusting the adversarial stage's account: filesystem allow/deny fully exercised (allowed write exit 0; denied read exit 1, 0 bytes leaked; denied write exit 2, host bytes unchanged; unlisted-path write exit 2, no file created) and network policy independently exercised against an owned loopback HTTP server (allow: curl exit 0, payload retrieved; explicit-deny and empty-allowlist: both proxy HTTP 403/curl exit 22; exactly 1 request reached the server), dated 2026-09-25, git-confirmed on current main (commit 6752ede5), with a self-review plus an independent_session review by a separately identified reviewer (model claude-opus-5-5), both 'agree'. So the candidate card's 'network denial not independently exercised' limitation is stale by one day -- confirmed by my own direct read. But the same receipt's own limitations say the test covered loopback HTTP only (no TLS/SOCKS/IPv6/DNS-rebinding/remote-host/escape testing) and nothing in it exercises 'broker execution authority' specifically. Since this layer's own requirement text is literally '...without granting research workers broker execution authority,' this is the single most requirement-central gap left anywhere in this layer, and it is real and still open.

challengers.name: Grafana Tempo
challengers.why_better: Not a replacement for any current winner -- it fills a capability gap none of the six winners cover: distributed tracing. Claude Code already emits beta OTLP trace spans (per this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep and observability/receipt.json) that nothing in the current stack ingests. Tempo is single-binary and disk-based (no Kafka dependency) and shares the Grafana query surface already adopted for Loki/Prometheus, so it is a same-vendor, low-integration-cost addition. This repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep already ran two independent adversarial-review lenses against it and neither refuted it (disposition: targeted_candidate, survives:true) -- the strongest-evidenced 'new find' surfaced anywhere in this exercise, yet it never appeared in the researcher packet handed to me. I independently reconfirmed it today: AGPL-3.0, archived:false, pushed 2026-09-26, latest release still v3.0.3 (2026-08-13) -- unchanged and current since the 2026-09-23 check.
challengers.evidence_level: source_review (repo-internal two-lens adversarial review, non-refuted; zero native execution on this stack)
challengers.trial_plan: Install Tempo 3.0.3 single-binary locally (the pin already checked twice); point the existing otelcol-contrib distribution's OTLP trace pipeline at it (the receiver is already present in the manifest; only a traces exporter/pipeline stanza is new, no second collector). Re-run a Claude Code or Codex task that emits OTLP spans and confirm the same trace_id is queryable from the already-adopted Grafana instance, with span count/duration matching what the SDK itself reports -- the same usage-histogram-parity discipline this layer's overturn_protocol already applies to Prometheus/Loki. Overturned if Tempo's single-binary local-disk mode fails the same restart-persistence check Prometheus/Loki already passed, or if AGPL-3.0 conflicts with a constraint not currently on file (none is; Loki is already AGPL-3.0 and accepted).
sources: catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json (grafana/tempo entry: disposition targeted_candidate, adversarial_verification.survives=true, both lenses not refuted)

rejected.name: Daytona
rejected.reason: Independently re-confirmed today, exactly matching the researcher's claims: license null (no SPDX), pushed_at 2026-07-24 (~2 months stale), latest tag v0.190.0 published 2026-06-23 (~3 months stale) -- despite 71,712 stars, the most of any candidate in this whole exercise. rejected.name: E2B
rejected.reason: source_review only, no native run in this repo. A credible microVM escalation path if a future workload needs VM-grade isolation beyond sandbox-runtime's process/filesystem/network allow-list, but nothing in this layer's current requirement or open gaps calls for that escalation yet -- sandbox-runtime's own remaining gap (broker-authority-removal) is a test to run against the existing tool, not a reason to switch isolation models.

rejected.name: Modal (modal-client)
rejected.reason: source_review only; hosted compute is closed/billed with no self-host path, fitting only as a paid escape valve, not this layer's self-hosted default. Off-requirement.

rejected.name: OpenSandbox
rejected.reason: source_review only, zero native execution, and further behind its own upstream than at last check; an unexecuted alternative to an already-proven sandbox-runtime with no demonstrated advantage.

rejected.name: cua (trycua)
rejected.reason: metadata only. Answers a broader/different problem -- full computer-use/GUI-level VM fleets -- than this layer's process-level research-worker isolation requirement.

rejected.name: OpenSRE (Tracer-Cloud)
rejected.reason: metadata only, public-alpha with a calendar-versioned pre-1.0 release train, zero native evidence. Would sit atop the already-adopted Prometheus/Loki/Grafana stack rather than replace anything; a watch item, not a trial candidate.

rejected.name: Presidio (data-privacy-stack/presidio)
rejected.reason: Already investigated and rejected by this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep (disposition: refuted_targeted_candidate) -- confirmed org-transfer via matching repo id, MIT, 11,009 stars, still active -- but it is a Python PII-detection SDK with no OTel Collector component; the pipeline's existing transform plus redactionprocessor already drop bodies/allowlist keys, and Presidio's own README disclaims full detection. The gap it targeted (arbitrary-content DLP beyond the single synthetic canary in observability/receipt.json) remains open; Presidio specifically is not the fix.

rejected.name: Vector.dev
rejected.reason: Already investigated and rejected by this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep (disposition: refuted_targeted_candidate) -- would duplicate the existing single-collector pipeline, and Vector's own documentation states its disk buffers force-exit on disk-full, undermining its pitched advantage; the sweep also flagged that its raw releases/latest API return did not match the version claimed for it. The real gap it targeted (the collector's own persistent spool has no automatic expiry and no loss/recovery acceptance under full disk or an extended outage -- confirmed verbatim by me reading observability/receipt.json directly) is real and still open; the fix is to fault-test the existing otelcol-contrib queue, not add a second pipeline tool.

claude_verify_checks.name: otelcol-contrib: receivers/redaction/exporters capability claim
claude_verify_checks.claim: 'Adopted distribution supplies OTLP receivers, privacy/redaction transforms and exporters to Prometheus/Loki without running a second collector binary.'
claude_verify_checks.note: Partly wrong as literally worded. Confirmed present in the pinned v0.161.0 build manifest: receiver/otlpreceiver (core) and processor/redactionprocessor, plus exporter/prometheusexporter + prometheusremotewriteexporter (all in opentelemetry-collector-contrib and the otelcol-contrib distribution manifest). But there is NO Loki-specific exporter component in this distribution: exporter/lokiexporter returns 404 at v0.161.0 and is absent from the full 46-entry exporter/ directory listing. Upstream CHANGELOG confirms it existed historically (present at v0.100.0) then was deprecated ('lokiexporter: Deprecate component', issue #33916) with guidance to 'migrate to using an OTLP exporter'. This repo's own receipt.json corroborates the real mechanism: Loki is configured to accept the generic OTLP exporter's structured-metadata output directly ('Final native Loki OTLP structured-metadata configuration accepted'; upstream_sources cites grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/send-data/otel/), not a dedicated lokiexporter. So delivery to Loki is real and single-binary, but not via a 'Loki exporter' component as the claim implies.
